source.title: Designs, Simulations, and Products for Rocket Engines
source.author: Tianhao Zuo
source.type: User-supplied survey; architecture reference, not a sizing handbook

applied.principle: Thrust consists of momentum and exit-pressure terms.
applied.implementation: Existing ideal nozzle solver; no historical engine performance numbers imported.

applied.principle: Pressure-fed systems use tank pressure rather than turbopumps to supply propellants.
applied.implementation: Selected architecture. Tank capacity, ideal-gas pressurant supply, feed losses and two equivalent injector outlets are screened; physical regulators and valves remain open.

applied.principle: Cooling, feed and combustion paths must belong to a connected cycle.
applied.implementation: One shared passage recipe drives PicoGK subtraction, inspection volumes, component anatomy and exports.

architectures.name: Pressure-fed
architectures.path: Pressurant → regulated tanks → valves → fuel cooling / oxidizer feed → injector → chamber → nozzle

architectures.name: Expander
architectures.path: Fuel pump → cooling → turbine → injector; coupled oxidizer pump
architectures.missing: Heat pickup, pump maps, shaft power and turbine pressure ratios

architectures.name: Gas generator
architectures.path: Pumps → main chamber; propellant branch → gas generator → turbine → separate exhaust
architectures.missing: Branch mass flow, turbopump sizing, shaft balance and exhaust model

architectures.name: Staged combustion
architectures.missing: Preburner chemistry, pressure hierarchy, turbine materials and shaft balance

excluded: Historical engine performance figures with inconsistent units or transcription errors
Generic claims that one cycle always has higher specific impulse
Product photos as dimensional CAD references
Nuclear propulsion discussion outside the selected chemical-engine scope
limits: This survey supplies architecture knowledge, not injector dimensions, fuel properties, cooling correlations, pump maps or validated manufacturing parameters. Vega ranks 8, 12 and 16 channel variants using explicit screening assumptions; the selected geometry is not derived from this survey or validated by it.
